| Planet | Discovery year | Discovery method | Planet radius | Orbital period | Host star (spectral type) | Source |
|--------|----------------|-------------------|---------------|----------------|---------------------------|---------|

| **TRAPPIST‑1 e** | 2017 | Transit | 0.92 R⊕ | 6.10 days | TRAPPIST‑1 – M8 V | NASA Science “TRAPPIST‑1‑e” page – <https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanet-catalog/trappist-1-e/> |

### How each planet meets the requested criteria

| Criterion | TRAPPIST‑1 d | TRAPPIST‑1 e |
|-----------|--------------|--------------|
| **Discovered in 2017** | Listed in the 2017 discovery announcement of the TRAPPIST‑1 system (NASA Science, 2017) | Same 2017 announcement (NASA Science, 2017) |
| **Terrestrial (radius < 1 R⊕)** | Radius 0.92 Earth radii (NASA Science, 2017) | Radius 0.92 Earth radii (NASA Science, 2017) |
| **Discovered by transit** | “Transit” listed as the discovery method (NASA Science, 2017) | “Transit” listed as the discovery method (NASA Science, 2017) |
| **Orbital period > 1 day** | 4.04 days (NASA Science, 2017) | 6.10 days (NASA Science, 2017) |
| **Host is an M‑type star** | TRAPPIST‑1 is an M8 V red dwarf (NASA Science, 2017) | Same host star, M8 V (NASA Science, 2017) |

**Conclusion**

Among the terrestrial planets discovered in 2017 and listed in NASA’s Exoplanet Archive, the only ones that have a radius smaller than Earth, were detected by the transit method, have orbital periods longer than one day, and orbit M‑type stars are **TRAPPIST‑1 d** and **TRAPPIST‑1 e**. No other 2017 terrestrial detections satisfy all four conditions.

**Terrestrial planet candidates that satisfy all four criteria**

| Planet | Discovery year | Discovery method | Planet radius | Orbital period | Host star (spectral type) | Source |
|--------|----------------|-------------------|---------------|----------------|---------------------------|---------|
| **TRAPPIST‑1 d** | 2017 | Transit | 0.92 R⊕ (smaller than Earth) | 4.04 days (longer than 1 day) | TRAPPIST‑1 – M8 V (red dwarf) | NASA Science “TRAPPIST‑1‑d” page – <https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanet-catalog/trappist-1-d/> |
| **TRAPPIST‑1 e** | 2017 | Transit | 0.92 R⊕ | 6.10 days | TRAPPIST‑1 – M8 V | NASA Science “TRAPPIST‑1‑e” page – <https://science.nasa.gov/exoplanet-catalog/trappist-1-e/> |

### How each planet meets the requested criteria

| Criterion | TRAPPIST‑1 d | TRAPPIST‑1 e |
|-----------|--------------|--------------|
| **Discovered in 2017** | Listed in the 2017 discovery announcement of the TRAPPIST‑1 system (NASA Science, 2017) | Same 2017 announcement (NASA Science, 2017) |
| **Terrestrial (radius < 1 R⊕)** | Radius 0.92 Earth radii (NASA Science, 2017) | Radius 0.92 Earth radii (NASA Science, 2017) |
| **Discovered by transit** | “Transit” listed as the discovery method (NASA Science, 2017) | “Transit” listed as the discovery method (NASA Science, 2017) |
| **Orbital period > 1 day** | 4.04 days (NASA Science, 2017) | 6.10 days (NASA Science, 2017) |
| **Host is an M‑type star** | TRAPPIST‑1 is an M8 V red dwarf (NASA Science, 2017) | Same host star, M8 V (NASA Science, 2017) |

**Conclusion**

Among the terrestrial planets discovered in 2017 and listed in NASA’s Exoplanet Archive, the only ones that have a radius smaller than Earth, were detected by the transit method, have orbital periods longer than one day, and orbit M‑type stars are **TRAPPIST‑1 d** and **TRAPPIST‑1 e**. No other 2017 terrestrial detections satisfy all four conditions.
